segments.line: You can't stand. You can't even crawl on your hands and knees.
You have to slide. On your stomach, like a soldier.
Mom goes first, dragging Biscuit by his collar.
You go next. And Ellie is right behind you.
Then she isn't. You turn your head. It takes everything.
Ellie has stopped in the middle of the yard. She's crying. 'I can't, ' she says. 'It's too heavy. I can't. '
Mo's voice crackles from the phone in your pocket. 'Are you in the water? Tell me you're in the water. ' You can't
answer. You don't have the breath.
Mom is already at the pool fence. If you go back for Ellie, you might not make it before nine. And at eight g, nobody moves at all.
So here's the choice. Keep sliding. Or go back.
Every inch costs you. Your arms burn. Your chest feels like a car is parked on it. Halfway there, you stop, just for a second. You can
hear the pool filter humming on the other side of the fence. It sounds a mile away. You
reach Ellie and grab the strap of her backpack. 'Hold on to me. Don't let go. ' You pull. She pushes.
Mr. Patel, lying at the edge of his pool, reaches out a hand.
and into the water. And for the first time in two hours, you feel light.
